entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6017"/><title type="x-s2">PSALM 48</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Ps.48.1-Ps.48.14">Psa 48:1-14</reference>. This is a spirited Psalm and song (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.30.1">Psa 30:1</reference>), having probably been suggested by the same occasion as the foregoing. It sets forth the privileges and blessings of God's spiritual dominion as the terror of the wicked and joy of the righteous.</title> <div sID="gen9173" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6017"/><hi type="bold">1. to be praised--</hi>always: it is an epithet, as in <reference osisRef="Ps.18.3">Psa 18:3</reference>.<div eID="gen9173" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen9174" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">mountain of his holiness--</hi>His Church (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.2.2">Is 2:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.2.3">3</reference>; 25:6, <reference osisRef="2Cor.7.10">7, 10</reference>); the sanctuary was erected first on Mount Zion, then (as the temple) on Moriah; hence the figure. <div eID="gen9174" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: PSALM 48 Psa 48:1-14 . This is a spirited Psalm and song (compare Psa 30:1 ), having probably been suggested by the same occasion as the foregoing. It sets forth the privileges and blessings of God's spiritual dominion as the terror of the wicked and joy of the righteous. 1. to be praised-- always: it is an epithet, as in Psa 18:3 . mountain of his holiness-- His Church (compare Is 2:2 , 3 ; 25:6, 7, 10 ); the sanctuary was erected first on Mount Zion, then (as the temple) on Moriah; hence the figure.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6020"/><div sID="gen9180" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6020"/><hi type="bold">4-6. For--</hi>The reason is given. Though the kings (perhaps of Moab and Ammon, compare <reference osisRef="Ps.83.3-Ps.83.5">Psa 83:3-5</reference>) combined, a conviction of God's presence with His people, evinced by the unusual courage with which the prophets (compare <reference osisRef="2Chr.20.12-2Chr.20.20">2Ch 20:12-20</reference>) had inspired them, seized on their minds, and smitten with sudden and intense alarm, they fled astonished. <div eID="gen9180" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 4-6. For-- The reason is given. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6026"/><div sID="gen9189" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6026"/>12-14. The call to survey Zion, or the Church, as a fortified city, is designed to suggest "how well our God secures His fold." This security is perpetual, and its pledge is His guidance through this life. <chapter eID="Ps.48"/>
